title: Space to Ground: Making a Global Impact: April 21, 2023
description: NASA's Space to Ground is your weekly update on what's happening aboard the International Space Station.
keywords: International Space Station, SpaceX CRS-27, Russian Spacewalk, Earth Day 2023
via: the NASA Image and Video Library

transcript.text: WELCOME TO SPACE TO GROUND, I’M NILUFAR RAMJI.
THE 27TH SPACEX CARGO RETURN, A WALK IN SPACE AND CELEBRATING OUR HOME PLANET.
ITS SPACE TO GROUND, THE EARTH DAY EDITION.
4300 POUNDS OF SCIENCE AND CARGO RETURNED TO EARTH
ON SATURDAY, APRIL 15 ABOARD SPACEX’S UNCREWED DRAGON SPACECRAFT
WHICH SPLASHED DOWN OFF THE COAST OF TAMPA, FLORIDA.
AMONG THE SCIENCE, FROZEN DWARF TOMATOES THAT WERE HARVESTED
WILL BE EXAMINED FOR THE EFFECTS OF LIGHT QUALITY
AND FERTILIZER ON FRUIT PRODUCTION, MICROBIAL SAFETY AND NUTRITIONAL VALUE.
ON TUESDAY, TWO RUSSIAN COSMONAUTS TOOK A WALK IN SPACE TO MOVE A RADIATOR.
THIS WAS THE FIRST OF THREE SPACEWALKS FOR EXPEDITION 69 COMMANDER SERGEY PROKOPYEV
AND FLIGHT ENGINEER DMITRI PETELIN,
WHO EXITED THE POISK MODULE TO MOVE A RADIATOR
FROM THE RASSVET MODULE TO THE NAUKA SCIENCE MODULE.
A PAIR OF ASTRONAUTS WILL EXIT THE HATCH ON APRIL 28
TO PREPARE THE SPACE STATION FOR CONTINUED SOLAR ARRAY UPGRADES.
YOU CAN LEARN MORE ABOUT THE SPACEWALK
DURING OUR PREVIEW BRIEFING ON MONDAY, APRIL 24 AT 2 PM EASTERN.
FOR ALL UPCOMING SPACEWALKS, YOU CAN CATCH LIVE COVERAGE
ON NASA TV, ON THE AGENCY’S APP, AND WEBSITE.
250 MILES ABOVE OUR HOME PLANET SITS THE INTERNATIONAL SPACE STATION
WITH SIXTEEN SUNRISES AND SUNSETS A DAY,
WE HAVE BEEN ABLE TO STUDY OUR PLANET
FROM MULTIPLE LOCATIONS AND DURING THE DAY AND NIGHT.
AS WE CELEBRATE EARTH DAY ON SATURDAY,
WE CONTINUE TO FOCUS ON THE WELL BEING OF OUR PLANET,
INCLUDING HOW HUMANS ARE AFFECTING ITS CLIMATE.
ASTRONAUTS AND INSTRUMENTS ABOARD THE SPACE STATION
HAVE THE ABILITY TO TRACK FACTORS INFLUENCING CLIMATE
OVER LONG PERIODS AND THE DATA GATHERED HELPS
INFORM CLIMATE DECISIONS THAT HELP US UNDERSTAND AND CARE FOR OUR PLANET.
ECOSTRESS, AN INSTRUMENT ON THE EXTERIOR OF THE SPACE STATION
MEASURES THE TEMPERATURE ON THE GROUND
WHICH IS HOTTER DURING THE DAY THAN THE AIR.
URBAN SURFACES LIKE CONCRETE ARE OFTEN
MUCH HOTTER THAN A FIELD FOR EXAMPLE.
THIS IS ONE OF THE WAYS URBAN HEAT EXPERTS HAVE NOTED THAT
EXTREME TEMPERATURES CAN BE DEADLY DUE TO AN URBAN HEAT ISLAND EFFECT.
THIS IS WHEN TEMPERATURES DO NOT DROP SUFFICIENTLY AT NIGHT.
WITH MORE THAN 3.5 MILLION IMAGES OF EARTH TAKEN BY CREW FROM THE SPACE STATION,
CREW EARTH OBSERVATIONS IS ONE OF THE LONGEST RUNNING RECORDS
OF HOW OUR PLANET CHANGES OVER TIME.
AT THE MOMENT, THE PROGRAM SUPPORTS A NUMBER OF STUDIES,
INCLUDING OF URBAN NIGHT LIGHTING, GLACIERS AND VOLCANOES,
AND ATMOSPHERIC PROCESSES AFFECTED BY VOLCANIC ERUPTIONS.
FOR MORE ON THE SCIENCE TAKING PLACE ABOARD THE SPACE STATION,
DON’T FORGET TO FOLLOW ISS_RESEARCH.
THAT’S SPACE TO GROUND FOR THIS WEEK.
THANKS SO MUCH FOR WATCHING.
WE HOPE THAT YOU HAVE A HAPPY EARTH DAY, AND WE'LL SEE YOU NEXT WEEK.
